summary.budget_rule: D-010: 28 generated frames per episode; extra shots are second framings of approved frames at camera scale 1.3 or less. D-017: if flat 2D frames average over 150 s across wave 1, Series 2 drops to 24; the four shots to fold first are listed under contingency.

generation_order: ANCHOR CHECK (D-015 rule 7): the frame check passes the five anchors before any other frame of their scene is generated.
SECOND FRAMINGS, no Codex call, after their source frame is approved: s04<-s09, s08<-s03, s20<-s14, s21<-s19, s24<-s17, s25<-s23, s27<-s07, s33<-s31, s35<-s31

ref_legend.nirala: <repo>/content/series2/refs/nirala.png (character sheet, period 1, medal drawn on it)
ref_legend.real_thana: <repo>/content/series2/refs/real_thana.png (plate, thana_day; also the series style frame, D-021)

method_notes: Refs are attached with -i in the order listed (D-013 rule 1 as briefed: character or pair sheet, plate, prop sheets, then scene anchor or style frame last). Each prompt labels them Image 1..N in that order. Do not reorder or drop a ref without rebuilding the prompt.

Every prompt carries, in order: opening line; reference labels (with 'do not copy from the anchor' items, D-017 rule 4); THE SHOT in picture-side wording; SAFE AREAS; the STATE block for the beat; CHARACTER LOCK = style.json character_lock + wardrobe_locks.p1 verbatim for every principal whose face or body is in shot; the pair's two_shot_rule verbatim when both are in frame; the grade LIGHT line for the beat; style_block and negative_rules verbatim (style.json usage_notes order).

Sides are written in picture terms with the character's own side named once. Nandini: pouch RIGHT hip, pen LEFT pocket, token RIGHT hand/wrist, helmet LEFT arm. Nirala: medal LEFT chest, holster RIGHT hip. Tripathi: gamchha LEFT shoulder, cone LEFT hand. Pushpa: wool ball RIGHT pocket, bag LEFT shoulder.

Script words that the style forbids are translated to picture terms: 'soft' and 'soft focus' backgrounds become 'a smaller, simpler, flatter background layer, no blur'; 'silhouettes' become flat single-tone featureless shapes; overlays (ov_token_7, ov_fake_board, ov_shield, ov_refusal_date) get a blank, front-on, unobstructed surface with its position stated.
Sheet faces per frame: at most two in every frame (D-021 decision 8). b7, b9, b10, b11 and b12 list three people on screen; they are staged as singles, two-shots and featureless silhouettes.

STATE source: continuity.json holds no per-beat ledger for s2e01, only characters.*.static and the s2e01 end_state. Each shot's STATE combines those with the STATE lines written in the script's beat actions (b1, b2, b6, b12) and the writer's staging note. Where the beat changes a state, the change is stated in the shot.

No prompt contradicts its sheet. Where an action needs a hand the lock calls empty (Tripathi's right hand in s18 and s22, Pushpa's hands in s16, s23), the lock is still quoted verbatim and one bracketed sentence after it says the STATE governs that hand.

cut_on_word.why: Clarity remap (S7, 26 Nov): beat b6 action cuts s13 to s14 on 'Zero' in both languages; the clarity l09 has no 'Look' and its English runs about 9.1 s, so s13 carries the head (about 5.8 s English) and the shield insert s14 the tail 'Zero crime ...'.

edit_notes_for_episode_editor.second_framings: For each shot with generate=false: (1) after the source frame is approved, copy frames/<source>.png to frames/<shot>.png (build_timeline.py needs frames/<shot>.png to exist, otherwise the shot becomes a slate); (2) put the shot's 'move' object from this file into edit.json shots.<shot>.move. shots.json sets camera_move 'custom'; without the edit.json move the builder shows the source frame unscaled, which is a safe fallback. Every scale is 1.3 or less (D-010).
edit_notes_for_episode_editor.voice_takes: l18 (hi, en) and l23 (hi) use take 2. review.json holds verdicts for take 1 only, so the take-2 files have not had a recorded review; S10 should review them before the cut.
